title: Finite-window simulation by a Turing machine
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean work-tape symbols, and let $T$ be a finite set with decidable equality. Suppose an update rule $u:T\times(\{0,1\}\cup\{\mathrm{blank}\})\to T$ satisfies $u(\tau,\mathrm{blank})=\tau$ for every $\tau\in T$. There exist a natural number $K$, a finite state set $P$ with decidable equality, a machine $R$ with $K+2$ work tapes over an alphabet encoding Boolean digits, work-tape cells, states, and tags, an entry state $p_{\mathrm{in}}$, an injective map $e$ from the three outcomes halted, left, and exhausted to states of $P$, and a natural number $C$, such that every $e(o)$ differs from $p_{\mathrm{in}}$. For every Boolean input $x$, window size $s$, configuration $c$ of $M$ whose work-tape heads lie within distance $s$ of zero and whose tapes are blank outside that window, tag $\tau\in T$, Boolean word $w$, and initial configuration $d$ of $R$ on the digit encoding of $x$, assume that $d$ is in state $p_{\mathrm{in}}$, tape 0 records the encoded configuration $c$ and tag $\tau$, the last tape agrees with the digit encoding of $w$ at every offset from $-1$ through $|w|$, and every other tape is blank. Then there are a time $t$ and an outcome $o$ such that $t\le 5V(w)+2|w|+3$, where $V(w)$ is the base-two value of the digits of $w$ in their given order; at time $t$, $R$ is in state $e(o)$, and it was in no state $e(o')$ at any earlier time. Up to time $t$, each work-tape head moves by at most $C(L+|w|+1)$ from its initial position, the output is unchanged, and the total number of work-tape cells visited is at most $(K+2)(2C(L+|w|+1)+1)$, where $L=k(2s+1)+\operatorname{posWidth}(|x|)+k+4$ and $k$ is the number of work tapes of $M$. For every natural number $N$, if the windowed run of $M$ for $N$ steps has an outcome other than exhausted and $CN(L+|x|+1)\le V(w)$, then $o$ is that outcome. If $o$ is not exhausted, there is some $N$ for which the windowed run has outcome $o$; at time $t$, tape 0 records its resulting configuration and updated tag, and the last tape agrees, at every integer cell, with the original tape patched by a Boolean word of length $|w|$ at its initial head position; all other parts of $R$'s configuration are unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite machine over Boolean symbols
$T$ is finite and has decidable equality
The update rule leaves the tag unchanged on blank output
$c$ has all work heads within distance $s$ of zero
$c$ has blank work-tape cells outside that window
$d$ starts in the designated entry state
Tape 0 records the encoding of $c$ and $\tau$
The last tape agrees with the encoding of $w$ at offsets from $-1$ through $|w|$
Every tape other than tape 0 and the last tape is blank
